question: How many students are in each project group?
response: The syllabus does not say how many students are in a group. It does say the Discord bot project is done as a team, and that the group work exists to practice the processes of working together to write code.

question: Is attendance taken at the open lab sessions?
response: The syllabus does not mention attendance being taken at open lab. It describes open lab periods as optional: time to ask questions and to work on assignments with help at hand, announced in the weekly email and on Discord.

question: Is there a dress code for the live demo?
response: The syllabus does not mention a dress code for the live demo. What it does say about the demo is that the full group should be present and prepared, that slides are not necessary but a view of the bot in action is, and that you present from your own laptop by joining a Zoom room and screensharing while the podium computer drives the projector.

question: Is there a minimum GPA I have to keep to stay enrolled in this course?
sourceSection: Course Catalog Description / Your Presence in Class
response: The syllabus does not mention a minimum GPA for staying enrolled in the course.

question: How many seats are in UW2 room 131?
sourceSection: Course Meetings / Your Presence in Class
response: The syllabus does not say how many seats the room has. It gives the room as UW2 building room 131.

question: Can I record the class sessions myself?
response: The syllabus does not address students recording class sessions. It does say the instructor's lectures and class recordings are shared through Panopto, and it asks you to stay focused in the classroom and avoid distractions for yourself and your peers.

question: Does the instructor apply a curve to course grades?
response: The syllabus does not mention a curve. It sets the mapping from your overall percentage to the 4.0 scale in advance, with even spacing between the top and bottom marks, and says that doing the bare minimum is a high-risk approach it does not recommend.

question: Are there any lab fees I have to pay?
response: The syllabus does not mention a lab fee or any course fee. It says the readings are free of charge through Canvas or the UW Library proxy, and the open lab periods it describes are optional drop-in sessions.

question: Does the Reflection have to be submitted as a PDF?
sourceSection: Reflection on Software Engineering and the Bot Project
response: The syllabus does not specify a file type for the Reflection. It says to cite real sources that support your statements and to write it without AI tools.

question: Is there any extra credit?
response: The syllabus does not mention extra credit.

question: Which weekday afternoons does the instructor hold office hours?
response: The syllabus does not list office-hour days or times. The instructor's availability is on her calendar scheduling site, where you book an appointment; if none of her planned times work, contact her on Discord or by email to arrange another time.

question: Where can I park for class?
response: The syllabus does not cover parking or getting to campus.

question: Will the course reimburse hosting costs for my bot?
response: The syllabus does not mention hosting costs or reimbursement for the bot.

question: Can I switch to a different group after the first sprint?
response: The syllabus does not describe a way for a student to switch groups.

question: Do we have to make a minimum number of commits each sprint?
response: The syllabus sets no commit quota. During a sprint it says to commit often and test often, resolve your user story, open a pull request into the team's main branch, and review pull requests for conflicts.

question: Is a paid Discord Nitro subscription required?
response: The syllabus does not mention Discord Nitro or any paid Discord plan.

question: Are the lecture videos captioned?
response: The syllabus does not mention whether the lecture videos are captioned.

question: Do I need to bring printed copies of the readings to class?
response: The syllabus does not mention printed copies. Readings are linked online, through Canvas or the UW Library proxy, and you are expected to have read them before the class session they are assigned for.

question: Where is the instructor's office located?
response: The syllabus does not give an office location. Meetings with the instructor are office-hours appointments booked through her calendar scheduling site, and the fastest way to reach her is a message in the Discord server.

question: Can I take this course S/NS instead of for a grade?
response: The syllabus does not mention the S/NS or pass/fail option. It describes grades on the UW 4.0 scale, with each component weighted and your overall percentage mapped to the 4.0 scale.

question: I know grade questions have to go by email. Which address do I use?
response: That is not how the syllabus has it: all grade-related discussion must happen via Canvas, not email, and email in general is reserved for when it is absolutely necessary. For a question about a specific grade, book a private timeslot on the instructor's calendar within one week of the grade being released.

question: How do I schedule the makeup for the standup I missed last week?
response: There is no makeup to schedule: the syllabus says there is no way to directly make up a missed standup meeting. You may find it useful to share an update with your group, but it is not a substitute for taking part at the time, and having missed one you are more likely to be called on in subsequent classes.

question: What time on Saturday is the Reflection on Software Engineering and the Bot Project essay due?
sourceSection: Reflection on Software Engineering and the Bot Project
response: The Reflection is not due on a Saturday: the syllabus sets it for Sunday, December 14 at 11:59 p.m. Pacific Time, turned in as a well-formatted essay via Canvas.

question: Since Task 7 is due before the demo, how are we supposed to work demo feedback into version 2.1?
response: Task 7 is due after the demo, not before: the syllabus sets it for Thursday, December 11 at 11:59 p.m. Pacific Time and notes that this is after the demo precisely so you can incorporate the feedback. In sprint planning you reflect on how the demonstration went, assign a user story to each member, complete at least one, then tag and deploy version 2.1 and turn in screenshots of each new feature.

question: Where on Canvas do I upload the Task 4 architecture guide?
response: There is nothing to upload for Task 4: the syllabus puts the architectural guide in your main repository on GitHub, and the instructor grades it right out of GitHub. Every group member needs at least one substantive commit to it, and it should cover both system architecture and code architecture.

question: The syllabus bans AI tools, so is a spell checker okay?
response: AI tools are not banned outright: the syllabus permits AI-based tools such as UW's version of Copilot on some assignments, with each assignment saying whether and how, and all sources including AI tools must be cited. Grammar and spell-checking are not considered a prohibited use of AI even where other uses are not allowed.

question: Attendance isn't graded, so can I skip the case discussions?
response: Attendance is not separate from the grade: the syllabus makes in-class activities, including the case discussions, half of the final grade, and the discussions are where the instructor cold-calls and assesses you. If you must miss class, file the course absence form; there is no direct way to make up in-class activities.

question: The Bot Project tasks are due on Thursdays, right? What time?
response: They are due on Fridays, not Thursdays: the syllabus says the Bot Project tasks are due Fridays at 11:59 p.m. Pacific time.

question: Standup is at the end of class, so can I arrive a bit late?
sourceSection: Standup Meetings / Impact of Missing Class
response: Standup is at the beginning of each class meeting, not the end, so arriving late means missing it, and the syllabus says there is no direct way to make up a missed standup. If you must be late, file the course absence form so the instructor knows.

question: Since the Reflection can use AI for drafting, which tool do you recommend?
sourceSection: Reflection on Software Engineering and the Bot Project
response: The Reflection is the one assignment where AI tools are not allowed at all: the syllabus says not to use AI tools for it, warns that AI tools are notorious for fabricating citations, and asks for an essay only you could write, about your own experience of the course.

question: Where do I submit my reading-note answers each week?
response: There is nowhere to submit them: the syllabus says the instructor does not collect written answers to the reading-note questions. They exist so you can prepare for cold calls in the case discussion, and you are welcome to work with other students on possible answers.

question: What's the Slack workspace name for the course?
response: The course uses Discord, not Slack: the syllabus puts chat, questions and asynchronous discussion in the course Discord server, with the invitation link in the Class Setup Checklist on Canvas. If you can't find the right channel, ask in #general-discussion.

question: Since the bot project is individual, do I still need a group repository?
response: The bot project is a group project, not an individual one: the syllabus has your team fork the example into one GitHub project environment per group with a Kanban board, create one Discord deployment server per group, and each student set up their own Discord test server.

question: I can just email the professor when I'm going to miss class, right?
sourceSection: Course Websites / Impact of Missing Class
response: Not by email: the syllabus asks you to fill out the course absence form, at least an hour before class begins, so the instructor knows not to include you in the cold-call list. Email is reserved for when it is absolutely necessary, and Discord is the preferred channel for everything else.
